phase_counters.counter_scope: Events explicitly enabled at analysis entry and disabled at analysis completion using perf FIFO acknowledgements; startup excluded

reference_dispatch_counts.profile: original accepted baseline reference archive profile
reference_dispatch_counts.note: Only execute_ex-symbol indirect opcode jumps through r15; cold split or helper jumps outside that symbol are not included.

limitations: The PHP parity goal remains open.
Native measurements are available only on x86-64; no native lowering changes.
Whole-command instructions and analysis-only time have different scopes; phase counters are reported separately.
One additional annotated unsafe block is an extraction of existing live-frame operations, with no new unsafe functions or raw-pointer operations. The optional origin uses safe NonNull::from.
Prior exact opcode attribution predates the cleanup-bit baseline and is only evidence for selecting an optimization family, not a current-source performance claim.
Every valid time/control sample is retained under the user instruction-count priority.

prior_opcode_body_accounting.note: Exact recorded PC instruction costs grouped only when the executed/direct machine CFG is reachable from one opcode target without crossing central dispatch. Shared tails, setup and called functions are not attributed to an individual opcode. Direct conditional edges are conservative; this is a lower bound for each body, not an inclusive opcode cost.
prior_opcode_body_accounting.reference_note: Precedes the accepted cleanup-bit checkpoint. Counts identify candidate families, not current-source acceptance budgets.

acceptance.primary_criterion: retired analysis instructions with identical PHP semantics
acceptance.tradeoff: Explicitly accepted under the user instruction-count priority; timing regressions remain visible controls.
acceptance.safety: One extraction block, no new unsafe function or raw-pointer operation; safe NonNull origin construction.
